value.assumption_check: Load-bearing and settled by measurement or by his words, not left standing: (1) the ticket file may be rewritten by the question door — measured: the artifact door journals ticket writes with verb cast today (clearance.clear writes cursors back the same way), so appending to `questions` is one more journaled cast; (2) `spawned` required-explicit is my read of 'explicitly say the answer spawned x, y and z in some jsonic way' — the field already exists as `follow_ups` (populated only when CC passes --follow-up); the delta is that the door refuses an answer that does not state its spawn, so `[]` is a claim CC made and the journal shows who made it — a design detail under his words, not a spec choice (memory blocker-is-foundation-not-authority), recorded here rather than asked; (3) the /intent-born question binds to the intent berth path until /sorted's filing rebinds it — the rebind lives in the filing step because that is the one act that knows both the berth and the new id; (4) the sieve is a build_inspector sieve because that is where every other 'two records must agree' check lives (history_integrity, constraint_enforcement_holds).
value.builder_check: What a Haiku-level builder needs, carried here: the door is cairn/tools/question/question.py (open_question, answer, _write riding cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write); the ticket lives at CairnCommons/tickets/<id>-<slug>.json and its `questions` field is a list of open-<12hex> ids; the ticket write goes through door.write(path, content, verb="cast", why=...) exactly as clearance.clear does for cursors; `follow_ups` is renamed `spawned` on NEW records and the reader accepts both names on old ones (the four live records under 9adc6fddf185 carry follow_ups: [] and are not rewritten — Law 7); the CLI spelling is `--spawned none` or `--spawned "<q>"` (repeatable), and `answer()` takes `spawned: list[str] | None` where None is refused; the /intent side: open_question(ticket=<intent berth path>) is legal when the path exists under ~/.cairn/devices/skill_block/0/berths/intent/, and skills/sorted's filing step (the ticket write at SKILL.md §5) calls question.rebind(berth_path, ticket_id) which rewrites each such question's `ticket` and appends its id to the ticket; the sieve registers in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py beside history_integrity and reads both directories; the BUILDME gate (open_for) is unchanged — it reads question.ticket, and the sieve is what guarantees the ticket side agrees. Left to the builder: the sieve's exact lack wording, whether `cairn question list` renders the tree with indentation or with born_of lines (both are fine).
value.collision_check: Whys compared, none exclusive-and-terminal. (1) I-universal-addressing-and-bidirectional-links (Akien 2026-08-23): its why is that a link with one end cannot be traversed back when the far end moves or voids; this ticket is that design applied to one file-side link (ticket↔question) — not a rival, an instance. (2) The artifact door (30531f6e1c5d): its why is that a record changes only through a journaled door; the question door already rides it, and the ticket-side write rides it too — no second writer. (3) The question tool's charter edges (a) and (c): this ticket closes them; the charter's filed_edges are amended in the build to say so, through the charter verb. (4) Law 1 vs. storing both ends: storing a derivable value looks like re-deriving the settled, but the why of Law 5 (the address carries what a mind needs NOW, readable cold) wins for a record a human cats — the sieve is what keeps two copies from becoming two truths (Law 7).
value.falsifier_check: DONE when: (1) `cairn question open --ticket <id>` leaves the id in the ticket file's `questions` list, written through the artifact door (journal shows the ticket path in the same act), and a follow-up born of an answer appears there too; (2) `cairn question answer <qid> "<words>"` without `--spawned` is REFUSED; `--spawned none` records `spawned: []`; `--spawned "<q>" ...` records the born ids in `spawned` and on the ticket, each born_of the answered one; (3) a question opened against an intent berth path is rebound to the ticket id when /sorted files a ticket carrying that intent_berth, and the BUILDME gate then holds the crossing on it; (4) `question_links_agree` reds a hand-broken link in either direction and an answered question whose spawned id is absent, reads clean over the live corpus after the build, and a revert of the sieve lets the broken link through (hollow-proof); (5) the hollow reading finds every written file load-bearing. Horizon: one build. WRONG INTENT if the ticket file's journal becomes mostly link maintenance — then the ticket side is derived at read time and only the question side stored.
value.missing_check: Wrapped: the door's two writes (question side, ticket side), the rebind at /sorted filing, the required `spawned` field and its CLI spelling (`--spawned none` | `--spawned "<q>" ...`), the sieve's three predicates (ticket lists a question naming another ticket; question names a ticket that does not list it; answered question whose spawned ids are not open records born_of it), the renderers (list, inbox, operator show).
